solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some spin on local dispute will carry weight

parts.note: a wheel is a spin or turn, as in a cartwheel
a local is a British pub, and a pub is a bar
a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: Someone's slant on a neighbourhood argument is going to sway opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry weight' looks like 'be influential'; it is literal: the definition describes a barrow that will carry a load. 'Some' just links. A 'local' is the British word for your nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled barrow is a garden cart built for hauling heavy loads, so it is something that carries weight.

clue.text: What a twitch may turn into — be careful!

indicators.note: the letters of the words may be turned into something else, rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous tic might become a warning to look out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may turn into' rearranges A + TWITCH; 'What' just introduces it. The answer is the British warning 'watch it!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Watch it! is an informal British warning telling someone to take care or mind out.

clue.text: Follow directions and prosecute

parts.note: E and N are compass directions, east and north
to sue is to take legal action against someone

explanation.surface: Obey the instructions and take the case to court.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, so it means to follow on.

clue.text: Doesn't include signs of spring

definitions.meaning: read literally, the foliage having come out on trees

explanation.definitionFit: Leaves out means omits; read literally, leaves being out on the trees shows spring has come.

clue.text: Earnings do not begin for a long time

indicators.note: the word for earnings loses its beginning, its first letter

parts.note: wages are earnings

explanation.surface: Pay is slow to start coming in for quite a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is informal for a very long time, as in waiting for ages.

clue.text: He keeps a servant

definitions.meaning: someone who holds on to or keeps something
an old family servant of long standing

explanation.definitionFit: One who retains keeps hold of things; a retainer was also a servant attached to a household.

clue.text: Joyful shout of TV doctor given work

parts.note: Doctor Who is the long-running British TV science-fiction series
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A cry of joy from a television physician who has been given employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of excitement or delight.

clue.text: Put on an act in front of nurse

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or in front of
to tend is to look after, to nurse

explanation.surface: Someone is putting on a performance before a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to feign or make believe, to put on an act.

clue.text: Gun-support bearing

definitions.meaning: the wheeled frame that a field gun rests on

explanation.definitionFit: A gun carriage is the frame supporting a cannon; carriage also means the way one carries oneself.

clue.text: Trial meant to determine will

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: to determine is to settle or fix, read here as settling the letters of meant into a new order

explanation.surface: A court case is intended to decide the fate of a dead person's will.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a verb but is the legal document; 'to determine' is the signal to settle the second word's letters into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of a person's property after death.

clue.text: Love to indulge in abuse and make speeches

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
to rate is an old word meaning to scold or berate

explanation.surface: Someone who likes nothing better than hurling insults also gives speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To indulge in' only joins the two pieces in the surface. To RATE someone is to tell them off harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length in a formal, pompous way is to hold forth, a plural verb sense matching the speeches.

clue.text: Having leaned over, he'd caught fish

indicators.note: the letters of he'd catch and hold the fish inside them

parts.note: taken as written, without its apostrophe
an eel is a snake-like fish

explanation.surface: After tilting sideways, a man says he landed a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that has heeled has tilted to one side, so it has leaned over.

clue.text: Move to break concentration

definitions.meaning: to move off, scatter or go away in different directions
spread out something gathered densely, such as a crowd or a chemical

explanation.definitionFit: To disperse is to scatter and go off in various directions, breaking up anything gathered closely together.

clue.text: Powerful businessman Tony gets upset about company

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes about, around, the abbreviation for company
upset means overturned or disturbed, so the name is jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Tony, a big business figure, is unhappy about his firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful businessman' reads as a description of Tony, but it is the definition; 'gets upset' scrambles the name and 'about' wraps it round the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, influential magnate in industry or commerce.

clue.text: Obvious method of speeding traffic

parts.note: clear means obvious
a way is a method

explanation.surface: An evident way to get cars moving faster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a road meant for speeding traffic. A clearway is a British road where stopping is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearway is a main road with no stopping allowed, designed to keep vehicles moving quickly.

clue.text: Two things a lodger may require with a computer

parts.words: Two things a lodger may require
parts.note: a lodger needs a door key and also board, meaning meals provided

parts.words: Two things a lodger may require
parts.note: a lodger needs a door key and also board, meaning meals provided

explanation.surface: A lodger's needs list includes two items, along with a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' here is the meals in 'room and board'. The definition is loose: the answer is the item used with a computer for typing.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard is the bank of keys used for typing input into a computer, an essential accessory for it.

clue.text: One having a sea-view?

parts.note: a window that looks out onto a bay, an inlet of the sea, punning on a projecting window type

explanation.surface: Asking about a person whose house overlooks the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A bay window projects outward from a wall, and the clue jokes that it looks out over a bay of sea.

clue.text: Rose made arrangements to name date

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman called Rose organised things so as to fix a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a woman's name but is the past tense of rise, the definition. 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanated means issued or came forth from a source, like rising up from it.

clue.text: Extra work for being late?

definitions.meaning: hours worked beyond the normal shift
read as over the time set, past the deadline

explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is paid work beyond normal hours; split as over time, it means past the appointed hour.

clue.text: Comply with notice

definitions.meaning: follow or abide by a rule

explanation.definitionFit: To observe rules is to comply with them; to observe something is to notice it.

clue.text: Different points about very unusual beast

indicators.note: the two compass points sit about, around, the jumbled word

parts.note: W and N are two different compass points, west and north

indicators.note: unusual signals the word very is made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: Various places surround an exceptionally rare animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different points' means two distinct compass points, which 'about' wraps round the jumbled word that 'unusual' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a two-legged winged dragon of heraldry, a mythical beast.

clue.text: Wants to be out of the French sewers

indicators.note: the word for wants is to be outside the French article

parts.note: needs are wants
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone longs to get out of the French drains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains but means things that sew.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles are the implements that sew, so they are sewers.

clue.text: Cloth worker, one in a mess

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled cloth
a worker ant; ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A textile labourer has got himself into a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' suggests a muddle, but it is the military dining hall: sergeants eat in the sergeants' mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is where service personnel eat together, and an NCO of this rank belongs to the sergeants' mess.

clue.text: Type out a note in foreign country

indicators.note: the note goes in among the rearranged letters
out signals the letters of the word are put out of order

parts.note: G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Type up a memo abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TYPE into EYPT, and 'in' puts G inside after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: This North African nation is a foreign country from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Time taken by a secretary

definitions.meaning: sixty seconds, a unit of time
the record a secretary takes of a meeting's proceedings

explanation.definitionFit: A minute is sixty seconds; minutes are the written record of a meeting kept by its secretary.

clue.text: A league match

explanation.definitionFit: A union is an alliance or league; it also means a marriage, the match of two people.

clue.text: Issue forth abundantly

explanation.definitionFit: Water wells up when it issues forth; well as an adverb means thoroughly or abundantly.

clue.text: Prompt about going on day-shift

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: shift means move about, so the letters of day are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is punctual about starting the daytime work rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like part of 'day-shift' but is the anagram signal, and 'going on' places the jumble after the piece for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt as an adjective means quick and willing, the same as being prepared at once.

clue.text: Circulatory system made one walk to work

definitions.text: Circulatory system made one walk to work

parts.words: Circulatory system made one walk to work
parts.note: sounds like the body's blood system, but describes a round-and-round device that made prisoners walk to drive machinery

explanation.surface: Something about the bloodstream forced someone to walk to their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The penal wheel turned by prisoners' walking powered mills; the word now means monotonous, endless routine labour.

clue.text: Drunk has nap in cup game

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
forty winks is a short sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: An inebriated person dozes off during a sporting cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cup game' suggests a football cup tie; it is the game of flicking counters into a cup. 'Has' and 'in' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: In this parlour game players flick small discs into a cup, so it is a game played with a cup.
